'''Tien Dung Kieu''' ({{langx|vi|Kiều Tiến Dũng}}; born 25 October 1960)<ref name="whoswho">{{cite book |title=Who's Who in Australia |date=2019 |publisher=ConnectWeb |url=https://connectweb.com.au/pages/whos-who-in-australia.aspx}}</ref> is an Australian physicist and former politician. He was a [[Australian Labor Party (Victorian Branch)|Labor Party]] member of the [[Victorian Legislative Council]] since 2018, representing [[South Eastern Metropolitan Region]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/elections/vic-election-2018/results/seme/|title=South Eastern Metropolitan|publisher=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref> He was defeated at the [[2022 Victorian state election|2022 state election]].

Kieu, a child of war, was born in [[Ho Chi Minh City|Saigon]], [[Vietnam]] in 1961. At age 19 in 1980, he and his wife Liem left Vietnam as refugees on a [[Vietnamese boat people|boat to Malaysia]], where they lived in a refugee camp until they were approached by Australian officials and offered passage and resettlement in Brisbane.<ref>https://hildas.unimelb.edu.au/the-journey-from-a-boat-to-the-bench/</ref> Kieu worked as a labourer before enrolling at the [[University of Queensland]], studying a Bachelor of Science, specialising in Physics and Applied Mathematics and graduating with First Class Honours and a University Gold Medal. This began an academic career in [[econophysics]] which took him to the [[University of Edinburgh]] and [[Oxford University]], and then to the United States as a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright scholar]] at [[Columbia University|Columbia]], [[Princeton University|Princeton]] and [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], before returning to Australia to work as an adjunct professor at [[Swinburne University of Technology]] in Melbourne.<ref name="vietnam">{{cite news |last1=Wallace |first1=Rick |title=Leaky boat delivers a right to asylum |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/nation/leaky-boat-delivers-a-right-to-asylum/news-story/4edc85f869107e893f985b4fbef08192 |access-date=13 December 2018 |work=The Australian |date=4 June 2014}}</ref>
